compatibility.linuxQt: v1 writer + growing TS + separate TS + muxed TS segments + muxed fMP4 AVC/AAC + separate fMP4 AVC/AAC + separate WebM VP9/Opus

nonfatalCompatibilityTeardownWarnings: Windows Qt reports QEventDispatcherWin32::wakeUp after tests finished; process exit 0.
Private Linux D-Bus teardown reports a closed bus after ctest completed; runner exit 0.
initialCorrections: Windows FFmpeg writes rounded audible Opus BlockDuration with DiscardPadding, while Linux FFmpeg omits the field. The TOC duration is now authoritative, padding is subtracted once, and both legal conventions plus inconsistent hints are tested. Initial runtime exit 8 and MSVC exit 1 are preserved; final runs passed.

The first sanitizer test assumed a final BlockDuration existed on Linux and stopped at assert groups (exit 1), without a sanitizer diagnostic. The test now explicitly injects both conventions into a correctly rebuilt Cluster and runs on all four toolchains.
The first private Classic run used a stale decoderContainer=fmp4 assertion; it was corrected to webm. Failed and intermediate private tasks/stages were removed before the final run.

The final Classic cleanup succeeded remotely, but a local SSH wrapper output path accidentally repeated _bin and exited 1. A read-only remote verification confirmed task/stage removal and matching binary SHA, returning 0.
limitations: Exactly two required scalar VP9/Opus views of one WebM resource, 1 ms timestamp scale, finite complete Clusters and known-duration zero-offset VOD; no lacing, additional tracks, external references, linked segments, live/config changes or muxed VP8/AV1/Vorbis.
Publication copies layout/index snapshots; multi-hour throughput, maximum index capacity and worst-case memory have not been stress-tested.
Container/index validation is not full elementary-stream entropy validation; actual codecs remain authoritative.
Native decoded hashes and exact timestamp comparison do not measure physical output synchronization.
Windows application builds were tested with separate profiles; installed Windows EXEs/INIs were not replaced.
